title: Contrastive learning
reading: The slide states the core objective of contrastive learning: similarities between positive pairs are maximized while similarities between negative pairs are minimized. Alongside the bullets, a schematic sketches a two-branch setup in which a query image and a key image are each passed through an encoder, and their representations feed a loss. Annotations note that the query encoder is updated directly, that weights may be shared across both encoders, and that the key encoder can instead be updated by a moving average (momentum update).

visuals.description: Two-branch pipeline: 'Query image' → Encoder and 'key image' → Encoder, both feeding into a 'loss' block, with side notes on update rules.
visuals.assertion: Encoder q is updated by the loss gradient, while encoder k either shares weights with q or is updated as a moving average of q.

concepts.name: Contrastive learning
concepts.why_it_matters: Self-supervised objective that structures the embedding space by pulling positives together and pushing negatives apart.

concepts.name: Positive and negative pairs
concepts.why_it_matters: Define what counts as similar vs dissimilar and thus drive the entire learning signal.

concepts.name: Momentum / moving-average encoder update
concepts.why_it_matters: Keeps key representations consistent over training, as in MoCo-style methods.

concepts.name: Weight sharing between encoders
concepts.why_it_matters: Alternative design choice (siamese networks) to the momentum encoder.
